# aibris v0.9.0

This release completes the unified cleanup journey: guided Codex worktree
decisions and eligible classic debris now cross one review, validation, and
execution contract.

## Highlights

- The default guided route merges accepted worktree choices with orphaned
  worktrees, agent state, dependencies, caches, and other eligible classic
  candidates into one unified plan and review. All categories share one
  selection state and one overlap-normalized set of physical targets.
- Dry-run and deletion use the same reviewed plan. Deletion adds only the
  execution-evidence validation, final confirmation (unless `--force`), and
  the existing safety-aware executor and receipt.
- Scan-cache entries are now stamped with the identity of the scanner provider
  set that actually produced them. A custom-provider result cannot masquerade
  as default-provider cleanup authority; a mismatch triggers a live scan.

## Upgrade and compatibility

The default guided experience changes from a sequential "guided review, then
classic audit" flow to one unified mixed-category review. When a selected
guided parent contains a classic candidate, the nested row remains visible as
covered evidence but is not counted or scheduled as a second physical target.

Selection states keep their safety meaning:

- **Selected** rows contribute an eligible physical owner to the reviewed
  execution plan.
- **Reviewable** rows start unselected unless policy or the user explicitly
  selects them. A selected nested candidate never promotes its unselected
  worktree owner; the nested candidate remains an independent physical target.
- **Protected/locked** rows cannot be selected, and their hard lock dominates
  the complete physical component.

Existing automation does not need to adopt the guided UI. `--no-guide` and
explicit cleanup selectors retain the classic audit/executor contract.
Non-TTY blank input or EOF accepts the current defaults, `q` aborts the whole
guided flow, and approved selectors and safety flags must remain identical
between preview and execution.

## Safety

- Unified execution rejects partial scan evidence and expired cached evidence
  before mutation. It then reuses the existing overlap safety checks,
  Git-aware worktree preflight, mutation-time revalidation, and partial-failure
  receipt semantics.
- `--force` skips only the final confirmation. It does not select locked rows,
  override worktree safety, or bypass execution-boundary validation.
- Representative-home coverage and a sanitized real-home run exercised the
  mixed-category path. The real-home review found 14 items / 4.9 GB: 9 selected,
  4 reviewable, and 1 protected. It ended with `[DRY-RUN] No files were
  removed.` No deletion-mode command was run.

## Windows status

Windows archives are **experimental**. The supported shape is the `amd64` /
`arm64` Windows zip archives cross-built by GoReleaser and listed in
`checksums.txt`. Native users verify the SHA-256 and place `aibris.exe` on the
PATH; `install.sh` remains Unix-only. Pull-request CI builds and exercises the
native executable (`--version`, `--help`, isolated `scan --json`), home /
cache isolation, recorded-cwd volume safety, and reparse-point cleanup
protection on `windows-latest`. A Windows version matrix is not published.

See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/sungjunlee/aibris/blob/v0.9.0/CHANGELOG.md)
for the complete curated change list.
